big: Every March, people buy a fund to save tax and then forget it. An ELSS comes with a three-year lock-in, and the lock works in a way many buyers do not expect.

lines: I need to save tax before March. Which ELSS should I buy?
First a question: are you on the old tax regime? Then let us watch how the lock really works.

alt: Twelve monthly instalments each locked for 36 months from their own date
caps: Rohan starts an ELSS SIP. Each monthly instalment is locked for three years from its own date.
After that, one more instalment frees up every month.
A SIP is never all locked or all unlocked. It rolls.

title: What an ELSS gives you
stops: Deduction under 80C in the old regime
Lower market risk because of the tax benefit
The 80C deduction in the new regime
alt: A shield with four statements about ELSS
caps: The deduction and the lock-in are real.
But the fund must hold at least 80% in equity, so market risk is the same as any equity fund.
And under the new tax regime, there is no 80C deduction to claim.

q: Rohan begins an ELSS SIP of ₹5,000 a month. In which month does his first instalment become open to redeem?
opts: Month 12, when his first year ends
Month 24, after two years of instalments
Month 37, and then one more frees up each month
Month 48, when all twelve instalments unlock together
why: A year is too early. The lock is three years for each instalment, counted from the date it was invested.
Two years leaves one more year of lock on the first instalment. The rule is three years from each date.
Each instalment completes its own three years, so the first frees up in month 37 and the rest follow month by month.
Not all twelve unlock together. They were invested on different dates, so they unlock on different dates.

q: A client on the new tax regime asks for an ELSS to save tax. What is true?
opts: Without 80C, ELSS is only an equity fund with a lock-in attached
ELSS still gives the full 80C deduction under either of the tax regimes
ELSS can only be bought by people who pay no income tax at all
The lock-in disappears for anyone who chooses the new tax regime
why: Without the deduction, the only difference from other equity funds is the lock-in, so the choice should rest on fund quality.
The 80C deduction belongs to the old regime. Under the new one, it is not available for any investment.
ELSS can be bought by anyone. Its tax benefit applies only where the old regime and 80C apply.
The lock-in is a feature of the scheme, not of the tax regime. It stays for three years from each instalment.

q: A buyer says ELSS must be safe because it saves tax. How do you reply?
opts: It is safe, because the government stands behind the scheme
It holds at least 80% in equity, so the market risk is the same
The lock-in makes it safe, because you cannot sell in a panic
It becomes safe once the three years of lock-in are over
why: No government backing exists for a mutual fund. The tax deduction is an incentive, not a guarantee.
An ELSS must keep at least 80% in equity. The tax benefit does not reduce what the market can do to the NAV.
A lock-in stops selling. It does not stop the NAV from falling, and a fall can still show on the statement.
The NAV can fall after three years just as before. The end of the lock only means you may sell.

q: Which is the better way to buy an ELSS for the year?
opts: One lump sum in the last week of March
A SIP across the year, picking the fund for its quality
Whatever fund the bank agent mentions first
Two funds, bought on the last day, to double the deduction
why: A single March purchase puts all the money in at one price, and it is often chosen in a hurry.
A SIP spreads the entry across the year, and choosing the fund for quality means the lock-in is not a trap.
The first name offered is not a measure of quality. The fund is held for years, so it deserves a proper look.
The deduction has a cap, so a second fund does not double it. It only adds another holding.

pts: Each ELSS instalment is locked for 3 years from its own date, so a SIP unlocks month by month.
ELSS carries full equity risk. The tax benefit does not reduce it.
Under the new regime, 80C is not available. Pick the fund, not just the deduction.
